proposals: SEBI should publish its public-issue filings register as a downloadable dataset with a stable company identifier, filing type and date for every row, so independent captures of the same register do not disagree, as the two used here did at 417 against 437 rows.

SEBI should add an industry-classification field to each draft offer document entry in the register, using the classification the issuer already declares, so sector counts such as Industrials, Engineering & Auto’s 14 per cent of filers need not be rebuilt company by company.

SEBI should show, against each DRHP in the register, the date its observation letter was issued and the date it lapses under ICDR Regulation 44, including any extension, so investors can see which of the 391 filers are close to the 12-month refiling clock.

SEBI should publish a quarterly pipeline table counting draft documents received, observations issued, documents returned or withdrawn, letters lapsed and issues opened, so the 64 per cent of companies that have never gone past an initial DRHP can be explained rather than inferred.
